lines.text: If you jumped into a hole through the middle of the Earth, you would never hit the bottom.
It's Sunday morning, and Gus has just dug a hole in his garden, straight through the planet.
His neighbor says he'll burn to a crisp.
His wife says he'll go splat on the other side.
Gus says he did the math, and jumps.
He's pumped out all the air, so nothing slows him down.
Two minutes in, he's outrunning a bullet.
Nineteen minutes in, he shoots through the center of the Earth at twenty-two thousand miles an hour.
The walls are as hot as the surface of the Sun. It's a very good tunnel.
But wait. Why doesn't he go splat?
You see, gravity only pulls Gus toward the middle. So the moment he passes it, the pull that sped him up starts slowing him down.
Ever pushed a kid on a swing? All the speed it gains going down, it spends going back up.
So thirty-eight minutes after he jumped, Gus pops up in the middle of the ocean, on the far side of the world, and stops.
Luckily, he stops for exactly one moment.
Unluckily, he stops for exactly one moment.
Then down he goes again, and thirty-eight minutes later, he's back in his own garden.
So Gus never did hit the bottom. He just comes home for one second, every seventy-six minutes.
